Olivia Chow delivers her victory speech to her supporters gathered for her election results watch party at the Great Hall as Toronto votes in the municipal election in Toronto. From retirements to defeated incumbents, Monday’s municipal election saw some unexpected turns. Follow along for live updates and analysis. Alvin Tedjo, Mississauga’s mayor-elect, says the city has voted for change. Speaking from Celebration Square, where he is holding his post-election media availability, Tedjo said it was the “honour of a lifetime” to be elected Monday night. “We knew it was going to be a tough road,” he said. ” He said Mississauga residents were “quite bothered” by how personal the campaign became. Incumbent mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie traded jabs in debates and on social media, a feud parodied by This Hour Has 22 Minutes. ” Tedjo said he just got off the phone with Olivia Chow and is scheduled to call Doug Ford today. items.title: Ontario's Police Watchdog Clears OPP Officer After Man Fractures Ribs Fleeing Cannabis Search on Highway 407
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has closed its probe into a Highway 407 traffic stop after determining a man's fractured ribs were not caused by police. According to the outlet, an OPP officer pulled over a westbound vehicle near Mavis Road on the morning of Oct. 11 for a Highway Traffic Act violation and then found an unsealed bag of suspected cannabis on the front console. The SIU says that while the officer searched the trunk, a 36-year-old passenger climbed over the highway guardrail and ran down an embankment, where he tripped and fell. The agency reports the man was taken to the detachment, where he complained of chest pain and difficulty breathing. According to SIU Deputy Director Stacey O'Brien, a review of video footage confirmed no force was used by police beyond handcuffing him during the arrest, and the man's injuries resulted from his own fall while trying to flee.

items.title: The biggest winners, losers and surprises from the Toronto and Mississauga elections
items.summary: From ousted incumbents to wide-open races sparked by retirements, Monday’s municipal election was full of surprising twists. Olivia Chow delivers her victory speech after her decisive win in Toronto’s mayoral election. From ousted incumbents to wide-open races sparked by retirements and shakeups, Monday’s municipal election was full of surprising twists. There were winners and losers. Some expected, others shocking. Regardless of the outcome, Torontonians overwhelmingly showed up to cast their vote. While final figures are still coming in, unofficial city data shows nearly 980,000 votes were counted in the mayoral race — an increase of roughly 250,000 ballots cast compared to the 2023 mayoral by-election. Olivia Chow will return as Toronto’s mayor after capturing roughly 54 per cent of the vote. In Toronto, Olivia Chow won reelection handily. Despite a tight race in the polls leading up to election day, she earned the highest total number of votes by any Toronto mayor in history. She continues the post-amalgamation streak of undefeated incumbents and will serve her first full term as mayor, after she was first elected in a by-election. Beginning of dialog window. items.title: Olivia Chow wins Toronto mayor’s race, defeats Brad Bradford
items.summary: In today’s First Up: Alvin Tedjo’s underdog victory in Mississauga and the Calgary Flames snap the Maple Leafs’ win streak. Mayor Olivia Chow delivers her victory speech to supporters at the Great Hall after winning the municipal election in Toronto. Good morning. This is the Tuesday, Oct. 27 edition of First Up, the Star’s daily morning digest. Sign up to get it earlier each day, in your inbox. Despite polls over the weekend projecting a statistical dead heat, Toronto incumbent Mayor Olivia Chow cruised to victory on election day, beating challenger Brad Bradford by 13 points. Chow, who was elected to a truncated three-year-term after John Tory resigned the position in 2023, will now have a full four years to try to see through promises, including expanding school meal programs to cover lunch for every student and 25,000 new units of affordable housing. Star staff were spread across battleground wards Monday night as votes were being counted. More on that and analysis from experts below. Here are six things to know on Tuesday morning: The incumbent mayor rode a hopeful message about the state of the city and won a second term in office Monday night. The veteran progressive fended off a challenge from her biggest council rival, soundly beating Brad Bradford at the conclusion of a six-month race that centred on affordability and public safety. She won, too, in that she re-enters city hall armed with new supporters and a refreshed bench of progressive councillors. Though ally and TTC chair Jamaal Myers lost in Scarborough North, Chow-aligned candidates won most other competitive seats, including in Bradford’s old ward, which was won by a candidate Chow personally endorsed.

items.title: First Mayor in Nearly 50 Years With No Ties to Hazel McCallion Takes Office in Mississauga
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports that Alvin Tedjo's win in Mississauga's mayoral race carries a historical first: he is the city's first mayor since 1978 who never served under, or was, longtime mayor Hazel McCallion. According to the newspaper, Tedjo's victory over incumbent Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor Bonnie Crombie came with a wider margin than first reported, more than 20,000 votes ahead of Parrish and 30,000 ahead of Crombie with nearly all polls counted. The Star reports a University of Toronto Mississauga student and Tedjo supporter, Jan Durkiewicz, celebrated on election night by saying the polls had underestimated their campaign. According to the outlet, Tedjo, 43, said the result showed residents were ready for someone new and pledged to freeze the city's portion of property taxes for the next two years. The Star notes Tedjo will now lead the same council he first joined as a councillor four years ago.

items.title: City Puts Extra Bylaw Officers on Patrol as Mississauga Residents Mark Diwali With Fireworks
items.summary: The City of Mississauga reports it is reminding residents to plan ahead if fireworks will be part of their Diwali celebrations this year. According to the city, Diwali, also known as the Festival of Lights, is celebrated by many Mississauga residents and is often marked with gatherings, decorations, diyas, candles and fireworks. The city says anyone planning certain fireworks activities needs a permit, and residents are urged to follow the rules to prevent injuries, fires and property damage. According to the city, Municipal By-law Enforcement will have extra officers on duty during Diwali to help keep celebrations safe for residents and their neighbours alike. The city asks residents not to call 911 over fireworks complaints unless there is an immediate danger, such as a fire or someone being hurt.

items.title: Every Returning Councillor Who Ran Again Kept Their Seat as Mississauga Picked a New Mayor
items.summary: Insauga.com reports that while Mississauga voters chose change at the mayor's office, they kept every sitting city councillor who sought another term. According to the outlet, the only new faces on council when it convenes in mid-November will fill the wards 2 and 7 seats vacated by Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, both of whom ran for mayor instead. The outlet reports Tedjo's winning tally reached 74,479 votes, ahead of incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish's 51,853 and former mayor Bonnie Crombie's 43,191, while Damerla finished fourth with 11,500 votes. According to insauga.com, ten other mayoral candidates also appeared on the ballot but drew far fewer votes than the top four finishers. The outlet reports the City of Mississauga said late Monday night that all polls had reported, though the results remain unofficial pending further confirmation.

items.title: Tedjo defeats Parrish and Crombie by a landslide in 2026 Mississauga election
items.summary: Following high stakes mayoral race, Tedjo said he vows to deliver change and get to work. Alvin Tedjo celebrates with supporters on election night after being elected as mayor of Mississauga. Mississauga has elected Alvin Tedjo as the next mayor of the city, capping off a high-stakes race to lead Ontario’s fourth largest city. According to City of Mississauga results, Tedjo secured majority votes over challengers incumbent Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie. 79 per cent of polls reporting, Tedjo captured 71,998 votes, holding off Parrish who placed second with 50,097 votes. “People in this city are choosing change, have chosen change and we’re going to deliver that, Tedjo said addressing his supporters at Wildflower Event Space. ” “We didn’t want to do that,” Tedjo said during the media scrum.
